blocks.text: BANGKOK – Thailand’s Crime Suppression Division (CSD) officers inspected a care center housing 92 patients in Kanchanaburi province on Oct 5, after a complainant alleged assault and confinement. The owner showed officers a licence and maintained that the centre operated legally. The complainant told a well-known television programme that their son had taken them to the facility in Tha Muang district, where they alleged they were physically assaulted and held against their will. CSD commander Pattanasak Bupphasuwan ordered officers from its Subdivision 5 to investigate the centre, which provides elderly care and care and rehabilitation for psychiatric patients.
